intuition.title: Study context: One aqueous route and separate analytical branches
intuition.text: The quantified TAE method mixes 32 nmol TBA and 125 nmol lead acetate then injects 65 nmol sulfur feed in room-temperature open air. Water is a reported alternative with unresolved final volume. TEM drying, CD dilution and ultracentrifugation belong to characterization.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1, aqueous synthesis and Scheme 1; SI PDF p. 1, Synthesis of PbS Quantum Dots Using Thrombin-Binding Aptamer

intuition.title: Study context: Sulfur-reagent source conflict
intuition.text: Main p.1 explicitly names sodium sulfide; SI p.S1 prints sodium sulfate (Na2S), while SI p.S3 specifies S2−. The SI name/formula conflict is preserved, not silently corrected. Na2S indexes the printed formula and main identity, without resolving the inconsistent SI name or hydration.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1, aqueous synthesis and Scheme 1; SI PDF p. 1, Synthesis of PbS Quantum Dots Using Thrombin-Binding Aptamer; SI PDF p. 3, nominal synthesis description

intuition.title: Study context: Measured and assumed dimensions
intuition.text: TEM typical/majority 3–6 nm has no formal statistical analysis. The uniform 5 nm diameter is assumed only to estimate 430/860 nM particle concentrations. No lattice refinement or measured coordinates are supplied.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1, aqueous synthesis and Scheme 1; SI PDF p. 1, Synthesis of PbS Quantum Dots Using Thrombin-Binding Aptamer; SI PDF p. 2, Figure S1

intuition.title: Study context: Optical sensing interpretation
intuition.text: The authors attribute selective photobleaching to charge transfer in an aptamer/protein complex; protein absorption does not overlap QD near-infrared emission. Quadruplex and binding cartoons are interpreted conformations, not measured atomic models.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Scheme 1, Figures 1–2 and mechanistic discussion; SI PDF p. 2–4, Figures S3–S6

bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1, aqueous synthesis and Scheme 1; SI PDF p. 1, Synthesis of PbS Quantum Dots Using Thrombin-Binding Aptamer
bindings.caption: Mix 32 nmol TBA and 125 nmol lead(II) acetate in 1× TAE without EDTA at pH 8.0. Room temperature and open air are reported; no numerical temperature, mixing time or vessel is supplied. Geometry, dimensions and colors are original conceptual presentation, not measured source apparatus.

bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1, aqueous synthesis and Scheme 1; SI PDF p. 1, Synthesis of PbS Quantum Dots Using Thrombin-Binding Aptamer
bindings.caption: Inject 65 nmol sulfur reagent with vigorous stirring; the solution turns light brown. Final volume 280 µL TAE; approximate TBA/Pb/S ratio 1:4:2. Preserve the SI sodium sulfate (Na2S) wording conflict with main sodium sulfide; no duration or purification is added. Geometry, dimensions and colors are original conceptual presentation, not measured source apparatus.

bindings.source_locator: SI PDF p. 2, Figure S1 caption
bindings.caption: Dilute a QD solution by a factor of 20, deposit a drop on a carbon-film TEM copper grid, and dry before JEOL 2010 LaB6 TEM at 200 kV. Drop volume and drying conditions are unknown; this drying is characterization preparation, not synthesis workup. Geometry, dimensions and colors are original conceptual presentation, not measured source apparatus.

bindings.caption: Use IR-1048 dye and a 785 nm laser diode as excitation for the reported approximately 23% quantum yield. Standard concentration and calculation details are unreported. Geometry, dimensions and colors are original conceptual presentation, not measured source apparatus.

general_background.title: Formation from dissolved precursors
general_background.summary: When dissolved species become supersaturated with respect to a solid, nucleation and growth can compete with continued precursor conversion. Mixing, complexation and solution chemistry can change that balance.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Mechanisms of Nucleation and Growth of Nanoparticles in Solution

general_background.title: From a metal precursor to reactive species
general_background.summary: A metal precursor supplies the metal, while its ligands and conversion chemistry influence how reactive species become available. Stronger or more persistent coordination can slow release of reactive metal species, while ligand exchange can open alternative conversion pathways.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Mechanisms of Nucleation and Growth of Nanoparticles in Solution

general_background.title: Conversion of a nonmetal precursor
general_background.summary: Chalcogen and pnictogen precursors can differ in how they release or transfer the element during a reaction. Bonding, coordination and the reaction medium can influence the activation or transfer steps that make an element available for growth.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation
